title: Two renderings: J. M. O'Hara, The Poems of Sappho: An Interpretative Rendition into English (Portland, 1910), and H. de Vere Stacpoole, Sappho: A New Rendering (London, 1920)
ruling: Lee Sharks, 2026-11-07: "i think we need a sappho reception history ea-corpora, whatever's public. translators, scholars. theres some ground work in the archive, notes towards a future reader i believe. the seating can include everything thats publicly available as well as declared absences and pointers for material behind pay- and access- and rights-walls"; and: "sappho reception history + future reader frameworks and related".
seating: EA-CORPORA-36, the thirty-sixth seating: Sappho's reception and the future reader, 1652–1993, 2026-11-07

why_seated: Two English Sapphos of the generation before Lobel's edition (1925): an interpretative rendition and a new rendering, each with its own account of what a fragment asks of a translator.
research: The revision of Closing the Fragment (v7, a draft of 2026-11-07 for Alexanarch), whose §6 controls the January composition against the translators from Hall (1652) to Carson and whose §8 declares an exposure-checked panel; and the Sappho Future Reader framework, whose groundwork is Research Notes Towards the Future Reader (#1548: Part I the scholarly field, Part II the future reader in twelve strata), and whose reading by a signed-out ChatGPT on 2026-11-07 is seated as capture 0C3D (sappho-future-reader-framework-constitutive-materials-chatgpt-20261107).
